subtopic: CANCELLATION OF FARM YOUTH EXCHANGE GRANTS- REQUEST FOR UNANIMOUS CONSENT TO MOVE MOTION
CANCELLATION OF FARM YOUTH EXCHANGE GRANTS- REQUEST FOR UNANIMOUS CONSENT TO MOVE MOTION
speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, under the terms of Standing Order 43, I rise on a matter of urgency arising from the fact that for a number of years the department of the Secretary of State provided grants to the National Farmers Union so that farm youth could participate in an exchange program with farm youth in other parts of Canada. In view of the fact that the Secretary of State (Mr. Faulkner) has cancelled the farm youth exchange grants this year, therefore I move, seconded by the hon. member for Brant (Mr. Blackburn):
That this House urges the Secretary of State to reinstitute the farm youth exchange program under the auspices of the National Farmers Union.

subsubtopic: PEI DEVELOPMENT PLAN
speechtext:
1.	What is the total expenditure to date by (a) the government (b) the Government of Prince Edward Island for program under the Prince Edward Island Development Plan?
2.	What have been the principal areas for which such expenditure was allotted?
3.	On what date is the plan to be completed and what amounts will each government spend from the present time to that date?
4.	What is the estimated number of new full-time jobs created under the Development Plan?

speakeroldname: Mr. Marcel Prud'homme (Parliamentary Secretary to Minister of Regional Economic Expansion):
speakerposition: Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Regional Economic Expansion
subsubtopic: PEI DEVELOPMENT PLAN
speechtext:
1. To
November 30, 1973 federal contributions have amounted to $52,612,358 and loans provided amounted to $10,413,000. The province's contributions have been consistent with the cost-sharing arrangements as provided under the Comprehensive Development Plan Agreement. However the specific expenditures as of any date can only be obtained by an examination of the financial records of the province and this information is not immediately available through the Department of Regional Economic Expansion.
2.	The principal areas of expenditures were resource adjustment and development in integrated land management, agriculture, tourism, forestry and fisheries; social development in education, vocational training, housing, urban development and community services; resource supporting and commercial services for transportation, industrial waste disposal, manufacturing, processing and market development; implementation through plan management, staff training and development, public involvement and evaluation.
3.	The agreement terminates March 31, 1984. Under the first phase, a period covering five to seven years, the federal commitment is $88,437,000 in contributions and $36,563,000 in loan funds. The provincial commitment is $117,963,000 for that phase. Subject to further joint federal-provincial negotiations Canada may contribute an additional $100,000,000 and the province an additional $380,000,000 during the period from the end of the first phase of the Plan to March 31, 1984.
Order Paper Questions
4.	A measure is not available to indicate precisely how many new full-time jobs have been created under the Plan. Plan activities during the first years were concentrated on transportation, education, housing and government. The primary aim of these activities is the provision of the supportive social investment necessary for the job creating initiatives to be undertaken in the second phase. Expenditures to date have, however, been an important element in employment growth since 1968. Statistics Canada reports that 1973 employment in Prince Edward Island averaged 39,000 compared with 34,000 in 1968. The 24 per cent growth in employment since 1968 compares with a 10 per cent growth from 1961-68.

subsubtopic: DREE-ASSISTANCE TO FRUIT FARMERS IN NEW BRUNSWICK
speechtext: To what extent and over how many years will DREE assist fruit farmers in New Brunswick and what is the current status of this contemplated program?

speakeroldname: Mr. Marcel Prud'homme (Parliamentary Secretary to Minister of Regional Economic Expansion):
speakerposition: Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Regional Economic Expansion
subsubtopic: DREE-ASSISTANCE TO FRUIT FARMERS IN NEW BRUNSWICK
speechtext: Until now, DREE has been assisting fruit farmers in New Brunswick indirectly, through both the ARDA Agreement and the RDIA program. Under the ARDA Agreement, and Applied Research and Development (Crops) Sub-program provided the New Brunswick fruit farmers, through the provincial Department of Agriculture and Rural Development at 50-50 cost-sharing, assistance in research, planning and information dissemination. Some research and planning was carried out specifically on the apple industry. A second ARDA program, called Agricultural Resource Conservation and Development Program can assist New Brunswick fruit farmers, through the provincial Department of Agriculture and Rural Development at 50-50 costsharing in carrying out a variety of work under the following: Farm Development, Small Farm Improvement, Sub-Surface Drainage, Erosion Control and Stream Bank Protection Sub-programs. Under the RDIA program, DREE can assist in the cold storage, packaging and processing end of the industry; through incentive grants.

subsubtopic: RELATIONSHIP OF INFLATION TO LABOUR UNREST-GOVERNMENT ACTION TO CORRECT
speechtext: What plans does the government have in this inflationary atmosphere to maintain essential services and some semblance of order in the country as more and more groups are apparently deciding that since the government will not do anything to protect them from inflation, they have to try to protect themselves?

subsubtopic: RELATIONSHIP OF INFLATION TO LABOUR UNREST-GOVERNMENT ACTION TO CORRECT

speechtext: Mr. Speaker, the Leader of the Opposition should not get overly excited or panicky about the extent of the labour problems which are confronting us at the present time. subsubtopic: RELATIONSHIP OF INFLATION TO LABOUR UNREST-GOVERNMENT ACTION TO CORRECT
speechtext: I had hoped the leader of the House, coming from where he does, would have been a little less insensitive than some of his colleagues toward the problems faced by the working people today. But now that the Minister of Finance has admitted that inflationary expectations have a good deal to do with the upward pressure on housing prices, does the government realize that these expectations are also causing havoc to the regular collective bargaining procedures to which the leader of the House referred, and that these inflationary expectations are endangering the economic stability of the country? Will the hon. gentleman assure the House that some action will be taken, quite apart from any action with respect to the collective bargaining procedure? Will he assure the House that the government intends to do something to dampen and control the inflationary expectations of the country?

speakerposition: President of the Privy Council; Leader of the Government in the House of Commons; Liberal Party House Leader
subsubtopic: RELATIONSHIP OF INFLATION TO LABOUR UNREST-GOVERNMENT ACTION TO CORRECT

As the Prime Minister and the Minister of Finance have already indicated to the House, other measures are under consideration by the government in addition to the very significant measures which have already been implemented, and these will be announced either at budget time or when other occasions are open.

speechtext: In view of the fact that the Ontario government intends to pass legislation covering warranties on materials and construction of new houses to protect purchasers, is it the intention of the minister to pass similar legislation respecting homes constructed under the National Housing Act and financed by CMHC, and if not, why not?

speakerposition: Minister of State for Urban Affairs
subtopic: POSSIBLE ESTABLISHMENT OF NATIONAL WARRANTY SCHEME-GOVERNMENT POSITION
speechtext: Mr. Speaker, I take it the hon. member is referring to quotations appearing in this morning's newspaper from the Ontario minister which were not entirely correct. I have called a meeting of federal and provincial housing and consumer groups to work out a national warranty scheme. On Tuesday there was a meeting held by a task force or sub-committee of that group to continue this work. Some of the provinces were represented. I hope all of them will attend the next meeting to be held on May 8.
